plain: Never wrong; unable to make a mistake

webster.text: Not fallible; not capable of erring; entirely exempt from liability to mistake; applied to persons.

more.text: Not liable to fail, or to deceive confidence; certain; as infallible evidence; infallible success.

example.quote: In the United States, the executive magistrates are not held to be infallible, nor the legislatures to be omnipotent; and both, being elective, are both responsible.
example.cite: James Madison, Report on the Virginia Resolutions (Report of 1800), Jan. 7, 1800
